utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, there is an outstanding motion in relation to Witness 167 due to start giving testimony on Monday. Is there a possibility that the Chamber would receive responses today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We're in the process of filing it right now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- other Defence teams. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will join the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will join the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yeah, Your Honour, we will need to take a look at this, but certainly we'll final something today, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is not filed could there be --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: A courtesy copy, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Dzolic, you would like to start yesterday as I did yesterday with reminding you that you're bound, still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Mikulicic, are you ready to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzolic. We will continue from where we left off yesterday and I will ask to you go through a document which is D567.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar please bring up the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, this is a document dated the 16th of September, 1995, which the chief of the administration, Major-General Mate Lausic, prepared for the Minister of Defence and for the chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian army. This is an analysis of the use of the military police of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia in Operation Storm. I'll ask to you go through this document briefly and to tell me whether the statements I will point out to you correspond to your recollection, that is your understanding of the events in the course of and immediately after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please could we have a look at page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we spoke briefly about the military police units, which were called AT units, anti-terrorist units. These units had some sort of special training in comparison to other units, general units of the military police, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the anti-terrorist units of the military police underwent special training?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Operation Storm or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I mean before Operation Storm and in general. A special sort of training as mentioned in paragraph 2, saying that by means of training they were prepared for the stages of assault operations, the treatment of prisoners of war, the sanitization of the terrain and so on?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot confirm that. I don't recollect anything about these things. However, after Operation Storm, in 1996, I was the commander of the an anti-terrorist company in Zagreb, and there, to the best of my recollection, there was a training topic concerning these matters. But I can't be sure about all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that members of these anti-terrorist units of the military police were colloquially referred to as the specials, specijalne, the military specijalne?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on to page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In paragraph or item 3, we can see there is mention of the way military police units were used in the beginning of the attack and during the liberation of the occupied territories. It says that check-points were set up from 0400 hours to 0600 hours in the morning of the 4th of August, that 80 control -- 80 check-points were set up in the area of attack operations, and then it says that this was done to prevent uncontrolled entry into and exit from the war operations zone and to prevent the uncontrolled bringing out of war booty. You also told us that immediately on your arrival in Knin you set up four check-points at the main entry points into the town. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but your activity was, in fact, in accordance with the general purpose for which the military police is used at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After you established check-points at the entry to Knin, the fact that you did this was not your own initiative. It was the general way in which military police were used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Dzolic, the last paragraph on this page, which mentions the search and mopping up of built-up areas, larger towns, and areas along the main roads on the newly liberated territory and that this was done immediately upon the passage of HV units by members of the anti-terrorist units of the military police and parts of the general military police. Does this correspond to your recollection from that period?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, that's how it should have been. However, I don't know where and in what areas anti-terrorist military police were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on to the next page, page number 4. Mr. Dzolic, yesterday we spoke about how immediately after the liberation of the occupied territories military police units were established in the towns. You can see that the 72nd Military Police Battalion Split, established a military police company in Knin. That was your company, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And further on, you see that the 71st Military Police Battalion Rijeka established a platoon, a military police platoon in Gracac and in Donji Lapac, another one in Donji Lapac, right underneath that. We spoke about this yesterday. Does that correspond to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspondence to my recollection, but I would like to correct myself. It was -- it says here on the 5th of August at 12.00 noon that the company was established. However, I entered Knin in the evening, around 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But it was on that day, the 5th?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, it was on the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Towards the bottom of the page, it says that these units of the military police took over the carrying out of military police tasks on the newly liberated territory in cooperation with the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. And that's how it was, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can move on to the next page. That's page number 5. At the top of the page, it says that the military police concluding with the 10th of September, 1995, escorted and processed in the crime investigation sense 1576 persons in cooperation with the SIS, which is the security and information service of the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia and that criminal reports and special reports were filed to the judicial bodies, and then it says 659 persons were handed over and it says that this was carried out successfully in collaboration with units of the Croatian army and the Ministry of Interior. Of course I don't expect you to know the precise number of persons who were brought before the courts, but does it correspond to your recollection that the military police, in cooperation with the civilian police, carried out this type of task? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it did carry out such tasks, but as to specific incidents and cases, I'm not aware of any while I was the commander in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can move on to the next page, page number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, may I ask one question to the witness in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This number of 659 persons, what do I have to understand this number to be? Would this be HV military men, or would it also be RSK military men, or civilians? How do I have to understand this number of 659?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I understood the question, whether this is a collective report, a report on members of the -- whether it refers to HV military men or to RSK military men or civilians, I cannot answer that question, because I did not compile this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will come to that particular questions a couple of pages next.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dzolic, likewise, the military police secured safety and unhindered passage for convoys of citizens and military personnel leaving the area of the so-called area of the republic of Serbian Krajina after their defeat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm referring now to paragraph 3.5. That is the previous page. We no longer see it on the screen. Page 5 where it says that there were 16 convoys with 1600 passenger vehicles and so on and so forth, 1436 tractors. These were convoys secured by the military police, according to this document. Mr. Dzolic, if you're not aware of this, then your company in Knin evidently did not provide security for convoys of refugees and defeated Serbian soldiers who were retreating, withdrawing from the area.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, we did not provide such security. I don't know about such things on the territory of Knin, but this is a report drawn up by the chief of the military police administration. It covers all the units of the military police on the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I understand. We can now move on to page 6. In paragraph 4, there's mention of the participation of military police units in combat activities. And in paragraph 4.1 it says that a company of the 72nd Battalion of the military police, which comprised the anti-terrorist platoon of the 72nd Battalion and the members of the general military police participated in combat activities. However, you have already told us that you have no knowledge of the anti-terrorist platoon. Does this, however, jog your memory, as to the participation of military specialists in these combat activities?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but they were not on the territory of the town of Knin. As it says here, they were transferred by helicopter to Rovanska and that was the axis along which they advanced. They were under the command of Mr. Primorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Likewise, in paragraphs 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 there is mention of anti-terrorist platoons of the 71th, 70th and 67th Military Police Battalions which also participated in combat activities. We can now move on to page number 7. Mr. Dzolic, when we spoke with check-points, you see here in paragraph 6.1 it says that after the assault operations, the attack operations, the -- of the HV the military police set up check-points at the border towards the free parts of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in cooperation with the Ministry of Interior. Do you know of such an activity of military police units that in the first days after Operation Storm they secured the border between the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this information. I don't recall any such tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 6.2, again there's mention of anti-terrorist units of the military police. And it says that they were withdrawn from combat operations and from the 13th of August, 1995, that unit, either independently or together with the MUP, mopped up or combed the terrain in the newly liberated area. This is in accordance with what we said about their being specially trained to carry out such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on to page 8 where criminal investigations are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, in the second paragraph, it says that the military crime police, in cooperation with the crime police of the Ministry of the Interior, carried out criminal processing for 321 crimes, and then the crimes are specified. It says 13 murders. 18 cases of HV members dying accidentally. 191 cases of torching. 13 cases of setting explosives. And 86 other crimes, chiefly theft. Further, it says that of the known perpetrators of the above crimes, 79 were HV members and 274 were civilians. Mr. Dzolic, you told us yesterday that in cases where a civilian was caught in the act committing a crime by the military police or committing a crime together with a soldier, the military police could process that person and take that person to the competent body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can now move on to page 9, which is the last topic I want to deal with. In this analysis by the chief of the military police administration, at the end, the measures that the military police undertook and continued to undertake to raise the general level of security in the newly liberated area of the Republic of Croatia are mentioned. It says here that the measures that were taken gave certain results but that they did not completely prevent the perpetration of crimes, especially theft, torching, torching houses, and individual acts of murder. And in connection with this, on the 15th of September, 1995, in Plitvice, a working meeting was held of all the chiefs of the police administrations and commanders of RH OS VP units and do you know of this meeting, Mr. Dzolic, which was held in Plitvice on the 15th of September? Did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I can't say with any certainty now that I either heard of it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record this is a already been established in the document D595, the meeting in Plitvice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dzolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, on this page, the second paragraph under 8 reads in translation "the measures produced certain results but did not completely the commission of prevent crimes." I don't know, is it meant to say "did not completely prevent --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "-- the commission of crimes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that will be the exact translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, in view of the fact that you did not know about this meeting, I don't want to take up anymore time. I would like to thank you for your answers, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina and he will now cross-examine you, Mr. Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, in your 2004 statement at paragraph 31, you were asked some questions by the Office of the Prosecutor about a videotape of a meeting that was held by General Gotovina on the 6th of August and that you heard about it in the press. The first thing I'd like to do with you is show you that video and then I'm going to ask you a few questions. I'd ask you to pay particular attention to the faces at the meeting, because I'm going to ask you at the end if you can help us identify as many people as you can who were present at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the Court, this is a meeting of General Gotovina with military officers on the morning of 6th August at 11.00 a.m., in a conference room on top of the Knin fortress. Mr. Registrar, this is 1D26-0045. And we've played this in the opening statement again for Your Honours. We have translations for the booth. There may be a value to the Chamber to hear the actual tone and if the Court wishes, we can play back -- I will replay certain segments to him. If the Court wants to hear the tone and the inflexion of voice, we can certainly replay it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, were you able to recognise some of the faces that you were present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right now, can you tell me who you were able to recognise as present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, present-day Generals. I don't think if they were generals at that point in time, that is to say the commander of the 7th Guards Brigade, Mr. Korade; then Mr. Krsticevic; Mr. Royce. I think I see here General Blaskic. Then over here I think it is the minister of the Croatian council [as interpreted]. Then on the other side I saw my commander, my commander, Colonel Budimir. Then Mr. Cermak. I saw some other persons but I don't know exactly what their names are now but I know them by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General Krsticevic was the commander of which unit?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned your commander, Budimir, as present, and I'd like it take you back to a portion. This is at the -- the 3 minute, 56 second mark of the video. I'd like to ask you if you recognise that General Gotovina is directing his remarks to Mr. Budimir in this clip and then I'd like to ask you in this short portion -- I'll ask you a few questions about what General Gotovina says in this segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In this portion of the video were you able to see who General Gotovina was talking to there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is probably talking to the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Budimir. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You -- as a military policeman, what does it mean to you to hear General Gotovina say military police is the executor of the code of the armed forces and guarantees its application in the field?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that. I don't know how the witness can be asked to speculate exactly what General Gotovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He's not asked to speculate. He's asked how he understood -- how he understand this to be. It could be language which was used but we'll hear from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the question please be repeated. I don't know what it is that I'm exactly supposed to say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the video General Gotovina says to Mr. Budimir the military police must obey, it is the executor of the code of the armed forces and guarantees its application in the field. What do you, as a military policeman, understand those words to mean?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, in my understanding of these words it is supposed to mean that I should carry out all my tasks as a military policeman in accordance with all the legal provisions that require me to do that. That is to say all the tasks derived from the rules on the military police. And that I'm supposed to carry out my duties honourably, honestly and at a high level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would you have understood that then as part of your duties was to ensure law and order among members of the HV?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, again 2004 statement at paragraph 31, you say that on that day, on the 6th, "Colonel Budimir spoke to me and stressed the need to intensify our work and to work very professionally and to have a very forceful approach to our problems." Do you recall whether Commander Budimir gave you those instructions in the afternoon of the 6th of August, or later in the day?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was sometime before the top people of the armed forces arrived. Now, when this happened, whether it was noon, 1.00, 2.00, I cannot say that with any certainty. It was before the supreme commander arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this video be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection in principle, Mr. President, but we have another -- we have the same videotape at 65 ter 3780 and I have been told that it could be a longer version. We may be permitted to compare it during the break, I would inform you exactly whether there is more footage in our version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There may be more footage, Your Honour, but the OTP regularly -- we don't put in long raw footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that if a party tenders part of a book or part of a video-clip and if the other party thinks that that same material that it is better put into context by giving a bit broader image, then that that is usually -- that's usually then tendered and we could admit it then with more context. If that is what you seek to do, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is so, Mr. President. I just ask time till the break, I have instructed them to compare to see if there is more footage that would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, then we already reserve a number for this footage. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D792, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D792 is marked for identification. And we'd like to hear from you, Ms. Mahindaratne, if you want to -- want it to be extended, and then I take it will still be a D exhibit but then the broader version. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you were also asked some questions in both of your statements about Grahovo and about incidents that occurred in Grahovo before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, there is a problem in the translation of P71, which is the diary of the Split Military District. Actually I'm addressing the Chamber, not Mr. Registrar, but there's a portion that was not translated from the original. We have uploaded a translation of the missing portion and then we've sent an e-mail this morning to the OTP to check it and make corrections, assuming we agree that's it is missing and then to upload the correct version in as P71. But for right now, I would ask Mr. Registrar to call up 1D52-0022. This is the English translation. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now at a meeting on the 1st of August, in the Split Military District diary. I won't read everything to you, but in the middle it says: "The greatest problem in OG north," which is Operative Group North, "is the lack of discipline which is why we ordered unit commanders to pay attention to this and to strictly forbid looting and burning." And now that was on a meeting on the 1st of August and now I'd like to call up, Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 2916. This is an order from General Gotovina on the 3rd of August, wherein General Gotovina states that for the purpose of having a uniformed command and control of the units, "I order staff brigadier Rahim Ademi is temporarily appointed commander of operation group north. He shall perform the said duty alongside his establishment duty." Point 2: "The outgoing commander of the Operative Group North, Colonel Slaven Zdilar is to resume his duty of acting chief of infantry at the Split ZP command." Mr. Dzolic, did you have any knowledge of the fact that General Gotovina replaced the commander of Operative Group North on the eve of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that I knew about that. But I do know that on the very eve of Operation Storm General Ademi was at the command of the operative group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I would like to tender 65 ter 2196 into evidence -- or Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D793.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D793 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Some of my colleagues on the Defence side have already taken you through Mr. Lausic's orders, so I won't repeat that here. However, there are a few questions I think you might be able to help us with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I can call up 1D52-0023.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: These are the notes of a meeting that was held on the 3rd of August in Zagreb between officials of the MUP and officials of the military police administration and the SIS administration: "For the purposes of coordinating the action of the MUP, military police and SIS in the preparation of and during the planned offensive activities of the HV in the coming period." And it records who said what at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could turn to page 3 in the English, please. And page 2 at the bottom in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, under the paragraph in the middle of the English version, and at the bottom of the Croatian version, is what Major-General Mate Lausic said at the meeting. And in point 2 he said in noting what the problems were in Operation Flash, he says: "Lack of coordination (in terms of dynamics and distribution of forces) under specific conditions on the ground, which reduced efficiency and unnecessarily created the illusion that the number of members engaged was insufficient. He also emphasised that he had now authorised UVP officers," which is the military police administration officers, "to replace the commanders of military police units on the spot, should they notice any irregularities in their work." Now, Mr. Dzolic, when Mr. Juric arrived in the field, did you have any knowledge that Mr. Juric had been authorised by General Lausic to replace commanders in the 72nd Military Police Battalion on the spot, if he should notice irregularities in their work?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I do not remember knowing things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 1D52-0023 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D794.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D794 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I please have D269, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you will see on the first page this is the order that General Lausic issued to various military police battalions, including the 72nd Military Police Battalion. It was an order that was issued on the work of the military police, cooperation between and joint work of the civilian and military police and obligations of the military police towards detained members of paramilitary and parapolice formations. The next section discusses the fact that the order is being issued subsequent to the meeting which was recorded in the notes that I just saw -- I just showed to you and to implement what was agreed upon at that meeting between the MUP, chiefs, and the military police administration chiefs. And then General Lausic hereby ordered. If we go to point 1, which is on the next page in the English. It is it General Lausic that issues the orders under 1.1 to establish strict check-points. 1.2 is to follow the advance of the RH OS, which is the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia. In the depth of the liberated Territory with joint patrols and ensure law and order, traffic for the needs of the HV and the isolation and evacuation of civilians for their security. Let's stop at that point right there, sir. Did you receive a copy of this order, do you receiving a copy of this order from General Lausic or that it was passed on to you a similar order from either Major Juric or Colonel Budimir?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. As far as I can remember, I never received any order in writing. For me to see, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How would you understand an order to isolate and evacuate civilians for their security? In what context would you be isolating and evacuating civilians for their security?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would put them up at a particular place. As for isolation of civilians and military men, I was given oral orders. I can't remember exactly whether it was Colonel Budimir or Major Juric, but we were supposed to take all such persons to I think it was the secondary school, in the town of Knin. As far as I can remember, it had a big hall. I remember this big hall where such persons were gathering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was this for their safety, or why would you be escorting civilians to the school in Knin?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the following reasons. Perhaps some criminals, if I can call them that or -- I don't really know how to express myself when speaking of such persons. Maybe some criminals, such persons would do something and later on the Croatian army could be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Moving on to point 1.3. "In populated places by means of joint patrols ensure law and order and everything else as listed in point 1.2. The RH MUP will take over the security of vital buildings in liberated towns, while the military police will provide the required assistance." Now, you have testified that you did in fact set up check-points in Knin. Do you recall whether the setting up of check-points or -- let me ask it a different way. Who passed an order on to you, and when, to set up check-points in Knin?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was issued to me, as far as I can remember, by Colonel Budimir before I left from Rujani, in order to go to the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 1.6 says: "To set up VP platoons in RH MUP PU centres in liberated areas, and military police substations, the strength of a squad to a platoon, in larger urban areas for as long as the HV stays in them." Now, you actually set up more than just a squad or a platoon in Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who passed the order to you to put more men in Knin than just a platoon?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about the necessity of having a platoon in town. The only thing I know is what I heard from my commander, Budimir, that is to say that I should go to Knin and establish a unit of the military police there. I was given treatment at the level of company command, so I don't know who it was that decided it should be a company rather than a platoon, as was defined in this paragraph here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to the next page in English, please, which is paragraph 4 -- numbered paragraph 4. General Lausic ordered: "VP unit commanders shall brief all levels of command in VP units and all members of the military police on this order during the night and ensure that it is implemented." Again, I think you have answered this but let me ask you one more time, do you recall being briefed in Sajkovici on the 3rd of August, about this order that had come from General Lausic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, question was asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason to ask the witness again where you say that he answered the question already, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I specifically now asked him about a specific place and time that he may have had a briefing where this was passed or as more of a general question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you add anything to the earlier question, the witness may answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sajkovici. Let me ask him a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the evening of the 3rd, before Operation Storm, did you attend any briefings either in Rujani or in Sajkovici?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, just before Operation Storm, I attended a meeting that was chaired by the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And where was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as far as I can remember, in Rujani or Sajkovici. I think it is Rujani, rather. Because the command was there or, rather, the premises where the battalion commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what was said at this meeting in Rujani on the 3rd of August?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was then made aware of an order on attacks -- or, rather, the beginning of Storm. This order was not read out to me but an order of General Gotovina, I think. Namely, that action should start.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I just wish to point out on record the witness did not say it was 3rd August. He just said before, and however, Mr. Misetic has read into the record again that it was 3rd August. Just to clarify that on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, isn't it true that this refers to what we find in paragraph 18 of the 2004 statement wherein the witness, your witness in the evidence you have presented talks about the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, call up 1D52-0019.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this is an order from General Lausic. Yesterday or the day before yesterday, I believe, on direct examination if I'm not mistaken, you were asked some questions about Major Juric issuing you orders and you referenced one order that could you remember was about securing the facility in Golubic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at this order which is an order from General Lausic which is issued to, amongst others, to the 72nd Military Police Battalion forward command post but to the attention of Major Ivan Juric. And in the order of the 7th of August, in point 2, it says: "To evaluate a method of physically securing all warehouse facilities and establishing physical security of the mentioned facilities from 0000 to 2400 hours." Do you recall receiving this type of order from Major Juric and to the best of your knowledge is this order related to the order you discussed about securing the Golubic facility?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: A compound question, Mr. President. There are two questions in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To speed it up, could you reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does this order -- to the best of your knowledge is this order related to the security of the Golubic facility?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. What's the foundation? First and foremost, has this witness seen this order, when he was issued the order regarding Golubic facilities, was he informed person to what orders that order was being issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He's already testified he received an order from his commander, Major Juric, to secure the Golubic facility. I'm asking him to look at an order. He is a military policeman in the chain of command. Is this order related to the order he has already testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question. Could you please put it to him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you testified either yesterday or the day before yesterday, I can't remember, that you received an order from Major Juric to secure the facility at Golubic. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall. My order was a verbal one, an oral one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As a military policeman, looking at this order from major -- sorry, General Lausic to Major Juric, can you tell whether this order is related to the oral order you received from Major Juric?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it is related. It is a logical sequence. The commander in this case, Major Juric, on the basis of this order, issued that task to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that the Exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D795.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D795 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Dzolic, your last answer you started saying that this is logic. Now, is it just on the basis of logic that you answered that question or do you have any specific knowledge? Was ever reference made to the order when you received further orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, Major Juric did not invoke any order. Rather, sometime in the evening he came up to me and ordered me to assign a certain number of members of my unit and that we should go together to the Golubic warehouse and that we should take over the security of that warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the link between the order given to him and the order given to you is looking at it, you find that all very logical, which I'm not contesting. But I'd like it know under all circumstances what is just your logical conclusions and what you -- what you observed, whether by hearing or by seeing, as a fact. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, I'm now going to show you a series of reports from Major Juric to General Lausic. In the interests of time I'm going to show you the three reports and then ask you a few questions about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The first is, Mr. Registrar, D732, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is Major Juric's report from the 9th of August. It is sent to the chief of the military police administration, Major-General Mate Lausic, reporting on the execution of military police tasks in OG north by 1600 hours on the 9th of August. Paragraph 1 says: "A number of household appliances were seized and receipts issued in exchange." The second paragraph, last sentence says -- actually, the second line: "It can be stated that the situation in Benkovac and Obrovac is now under control except for a few cases of seizing of items usually seized at check-points anyway." If you can turn the page, please: "The VP post in Sinj reports that a tractor was seized from Lieutenant Grgic and handed over to the Vrlika leadership for use. A Labin Progres milling machine and an Agria milling machine were seized from Private Marko, and then his last name appears. You will note, Mr. Dzolic, that the report does not appear to be copied to anyone and is sent directly to Major-General Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next, Mr. Registrar, which is D733, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is again a report from Major Ivan Juric directly to military police administration to the attention of the chief. No one is copied on it. Again, reporting on the military police tasks carried out in OG north. Under point 2, reference is the guarding of the monastery in Kistanje. And also it says: "No violations of public law and order were registered in the observe period?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go, Mr. Registrar, to D211, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Same -- this is now 12 August and I'm going to take you back to the day before. I forgot to show you that one. This is the 12th of August. Again Major Ivan Juric reporting directly to the chief of the military police administration. No one is copied on the report and you will note that he says at paragraph 4: "In the crime military police section, no crimes have been recorded." "5. The VP have not arrested or brought in any persons." If we could go back now to D734. This is from the day before. Page -- this is at paragraph 4, and again it is Major Juric reporting directly to the chief of the military police administration. No one is copied. Paragraph 4 says: "In the crime VP section, perpetrators of crimes, misappropriation of property from the liberated areas are being processed daily." Now, I have shown you four documents, Mr. Dzolic. My question to you is: Through most of these documents you were present in Knin. Do you recall having to assist Major Juric in preparing daily reports of the work of the military police?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember helping him in preparing reports. However, I do allow for the possibility that in my segment for my own company I provided to him on a daily basis parameters for compiling this kind of report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you have to send reports to Major Juric on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall with any certainty, but I think that that was the way it was supposed to be. Namely, that I was supposed to provide reports to him every day, in terms of my segment of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the crime section of the military police submitted reports to Major Juric, on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I have Exhibit D595, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the meeting that Mr. Mikulicic referenced during his cross-examination that took place -- I'm sorry, the minutes or notes of a meeting that took place in Plitvice between representatives of the MUP and the military police on 15 September 1995 at 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I know you weren't present for this meeting but there is a statement made about this meeting, and I would like to see if it is consistent with your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This would be page 3 of the Croatian version, at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says that -- the people present at this meeting were listed on page 1 and they are the members of the RH MUP and the members of the military police administration. And General Lausic is reported as having said: "Members of the MUP and the military police are the promotors of the state policy and the only people responsible for its implementation are present at this meeting. The objective is clear: Protection of people and property and creation of positive security situation in the entire area of the Republic of Croatia." Now, this statement that "the members of the MUP and the military police are the promoters of the state policy and the only people responsible for its implementation are present at this meeting," was it your understanding, Mr. Dzolic, that the MUP and the military police working together were the organs of the Republic of Croatia that were responsible for the protection of people and property and the creation of a positive security situation in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who was responsible for providing security in the area? Was it the MUP and the military police?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I may have 1D52-0016, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, this is not a document that was addressed to you. However, you have been posed some questions about what daily operational tasks mean, et cetera. This is an response that General Gotovina issued on the 12th of April, 1995 to the commander of the Vrgorac garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the Court, just it let the Chamber know, we are still searching for the original request from the Vrgorac garrison to General Gotovina which we still have not been able to locate but this is the response and from the context it appears that the Vrgorac garrison commander had requested a deployment of the military police, and General Gotovina's response was at point 1: "According to the formation and the rules of the military police, military police units are not designated to implement tasks such as the one requested above." "2. The use and deployment of military police units for tasks of a longer duration as stated in the request by the Vrgorac garrison command are decided on and approved by the military police administration, i.e., chief of the military police administration in Zagreb." Now, I know you were a company commander, but do you have any knowledge of the fact that longer-term deployment of the military police could only be done by the military police administration?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, all long-term transfers or movements of military police units were -- fell within the purview of the military police administration. The commander of a military police battalion, at his level, could also transfer or relocate a certain unit. But probably he would previously need the approval and agreement of the chief of the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that this exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D796.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D796 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, I thank you for coming to testify and I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. The Cermak Defence still --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't catch all of that. The Cermak Defence still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to verify that. Matters can change sometimes. We will first have a break. Ms. Mahindaratne, you indicated yesterday that you would need a certain time for re-examination. Has the estimate changed? You yesterday said as matters stand now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, it is about the same estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I start, with regard to the videotape, in fact what we have is more footage. We have two tapes of the same meeting, and one tape begins much before the clip that was shown by Mr. Misetic and then goes on through the meeting, that part that we saw, and even after the meeting after what was seen, there is much more at the meeting itself. And then the second tape has further footage of the same meeting, so I propose, Mr. President, that we are permitted to tender both tapes so that the Chamber could view as much footage of the meeting as possible. I think it would place the clip that we saw in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously the Prosecution can submit its open exhibits. I have looked at what they have and theirs is, respect to things that I showed the witness, is deleted from the video on the -- where General Gotovina says the military police needs to be -- to its job, et cetera, that portion has been deleted from the Prosecution's videos, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The section that we're talking about here as I recall is only one of the two Prosecution videos and within that section the issue of General Gotovina yelling at the military police battalion commander does not appear in their video of that event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, replacing the broader version would not -- certainly not serve the purposes of the Defence, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, may I just say that on the contrary, we do have that segment, but I don't want to quarrel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not quarrel in court about what is in what version of a video. I do understand that the Prosecution would like the Chamber to look as broadly as possible to the video of that meeting. The Defence wants to be sure that the portion played in court certainly is in evidence. Now, may I take it that this matter can be resolved --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that the parties could agree meeting both wishes and then come up with the video for which -- and upload that, the video which was assigned already a provisional exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll talk to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Talk with them, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I meant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, are you ready.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For one reason or another, my screen on exhibit, et cetera, gives a nice blueish colour, which I like very much, but I even prefer white. Is there any way that this apparent technical problem can be resolved. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, now, your testimony yesterday was that on 20th August 2008, when you met with members of the Office of the Prosecutor, you examined your 2004 statement and made certain changes to that. Now, in fact, you -- one of the changes amongst many that you made on 20th August 2008 was to paragraph 37 of your previous statement. And let me read out the correction that you made, which is recorded in paragraph 15 of the 2008 statement that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, to interrupt my learned friend but I think it would be helpful at this point if the witness was given both the statement in B/C/S, his first statement, and his second whatever euphemism is referred to, but I think the clarification or the proofing notes so that he can see what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I was under the impression it was in front of the witness. May the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't see it. If Madam Usher could assist so that the witness has both his 2004 statement and the statement of 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, could you take a look at your 2008 statement and let me take you to paragraph 15. And reading out, this is the correction that you made to paragraph 37 on 20th August 2008. You say: "In paragraph 37 I refer to General Cermak being introduced to me as a general and government commissioner. I should like to change that to a general and garrison commander for Knin." Now, that was the correction you made to paragraph 37 of your 2004 statement on 20th August 2008. Now, Mr. Dzolic, when you came to testify on Wednesday, about what time were you brought into this building?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little before the session began, some 20 minutes before, or half an hour before the beginning of the session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at that time you were given your two statements, is that correct, to peruse?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you came into court, you informed court that you did not have -- have the opportunity to examine your 2008 statement and that you wished to in fact examine the 2008 statement prior to confirming the accuracy of the contents?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when it was -- when Mr. Kay put it to you or asked you if you agreed that in -- that the contents in paragraph 37 of your 2004 statement and let me just -- I will be precise. Let me read that particular paragraph. Your statement to the effect that in paragraph 37 of 2004: "The way I understood it was that I was still under the command of Colonel Budimir and that I was also under the command of General Cermak and I was to obey any order that General Cermak gave." As to whether you -- whether you considered that an accurate statement, yesterday you said that you did -- that it was wrong. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can Ms. Mahindaratne actually read back to the witness what he said yesterday because all she's read now is the statement, and I think for the purposes of fairness to the witness it should be read back to him the questions and answers that my learned friend Mr. Kay put to the witness and which he affirmed yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President if I could take parties to transcript 9035 going to 9037.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, this is what you were asked. And you were read back that passage. And then you -- "are those your words, Mr. Dzolic, did you say that?" "The way I understood it was I was still under the command of Colonel Budimir but that I was also under the command of General Cermak and I was to obey any order that General Cermak gave me. Did you say that?" "I don't think that is the way I put it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, if you make always clear what the witness says and what the question was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your answer then to that question was: "I don't think that's the way I put it." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then asked a further question, Mr. Dzolic, by Mr. Kay. He asked you this question: "Is that statement wrong?" And that is referring to that particular passage we read out. And your answer was: "For a part, yes." And then going to page -- transcript page 9037, again you were asked this question: "Is it wrong as written here that I was also under the commander of General Cermak and I was to obey any order that General Cermak gave me." And Mr. Kay was reading again a passage from your 2004 statement. And you answered in court: "As I understand the statement, it is incorrect." You were asked this question by Mr. Kay: "First of all, is it wrong to say you were under the command of General Cermak? " Your answer was: "I was not under the command of General Cermak. I was under the command of Colonel Budimir." The question is asked again by Mr. Kay: "Is it wrong to say that you were to obey any order that General Cermak gave you?" Your statement was: "That is correct." Now, Mr. Dzolic, what happened between the morning of Wednesday and yesterday for you to change your mind that what you had stated in paragraph 37 of your 2004 statement was incorrect? What led to you change your mind?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, reading my statement of 2008, because there was so little time and because I was very tense prior to my testimony before the Court and before Your Honours, probably I made a mistake in that I did not notice this sentence as it is written down in my statement. I did not see at the time that it was erroneous. While I was preparing to testify, I didn't read the entire 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, I'm not referring to your 2008 statement. I'm referring to your 2004 statement. That passage Mr. Kay read to you was from the 2004 statement and on 20th August you made several corrections to your 2004 statement. In particular, you made a correction to paragraph 37. But you never, ever raised this -- the fact that this particular statement about not obeying orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting at this point. If the witness could remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you take off your earphones for a second, Mr. Dzolic. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think my learned friend has to be extremely careful about how she's actually putting this to the witness. We know that the original statement was heavily corrected in a clarification statement or in these proofing notes. We then know that the proofing notes were also incorrect. It could be that the witness is actually saying that when he read the correction in the subsequent statement correcting the original paragraph 37, that he hadn't noticed that in fact he hadn't also corrected that other part in the original paragraph. I mean, I don't want to interpret what the witness is saying, but I think we have to be fair to him because it's clear that there were a lot of errors in his written statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are other opportunities as well, Mr. Cayley. You hint at one possible explanation. There are other possible explanations and Ms. Mahindaratne will certainly be careful but is entitled to fully explore the issue. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dzolic, my question to you is: You did not -- you in fact made a particular correction to paragraph 37 itself on 20th August 2008. How is it that did you not correct it then but you did so yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember why I didn't notice that then, but probably because looking at this paragraph, I wasn't paying that much attention to the other paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, do you recall at that proofing meeting, you know, you said you read slow and you read your 2004 statement very carefully. And how is it that you correct a sentence in the same paragraph but not another sentence at that time, and now you're saying that you missed that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my mistake that I missed it. I don't know what response would satisfy you. I just didn't notice it at that time. I corrected what I noticed. At that time, I didn't notice this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on. You were also questioned about reporting to Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I have document P886, please, and if you could go to the English page 7453. English page 7453, page 8; and B/C/S page 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dzolic, if you could focus on the entry at 1305. There's a reference to a patrol reporting to -- being ordered to report to General Cermak. Now, can you say as to why military police patrols were reporting to General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I object to this point, can -- it doesn't actually say that a military police patrol should report to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's read literally.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. President, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me read back to you what it says and you can possibly read for yourself, Mr. Dzolic. It says: "Information comes from," and this illegible. It says, it looks like MUP, you can correct me if I'm wrong, to the -- to a person in the -- the duty station and it say: "Mosor 1 should report to General Cermak. " Now what is Mosor 1? For the record M-o-s-o-r. Can you tell Court what Mosor 1 is.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mosor 1 is probably a code-name used over the radio for the commander of that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What company?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the log-book of the 7th Company, then it would be the commander of that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you say 7th Company you're referring to the joint Knin company, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just make an interruption at this point, but I think there is a problem with the translation of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The translation issues are be dealt with when the witness doesn't listen. Could you take off your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: My understanding from my Croatian speaking colleague is that the word javni, which is being translated as -- javi, which is being translated as translated as report can also mean contact. Should contact. Which would change the meaning of this significantly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will upload the revised translation but at this stage perhaps if the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that the interpreters are not tasked with reviewing written translations. But of course I could make an entirely separate from that. The two meanings of the word javi as just presented by Mr. Cayley can it be confirmed that it this word has two meanings? I'm not asking to review the translation but whether there is any possibility that perhaps one is chosen where another could --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, Ms. Mahindaratne, now if you -- you can put the question again to the witness and now include that Mosor 1 should report or contact General Cermak. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put on your earphones again. We were dealing with a translation issue, Mr. Dzolic. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think I didn't get an answer from you, Mr. Dzolic, for my last question, which was: When you referred to 7th Company, that is the reference to the joint Knin company, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the joint company. But as far as I can see here, it is dated the 19th August, and if I remember correctly, when I left that company was given a number and it was under the command of Luka Orsulic. It was no longer the joint company but the 7th Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can you say -- or are you able to say as to why Mosor 1 is required to report or to contact General Cermak there at 1305?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this question should be put to that commander and to General Cermak, if he remembers why, on that day at that hour, he asked to speak to that person. I really don't know why he should want to call him, but it would not be in order for me to speculate now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I just move on. Mr. Dzolic, if you could look at paragraph 11 of your 2008 statement and in fact yesterday you were extensively questioned on Major Juric. Now, this is what you told us on the 20th of August 2008 about Major Juric and in fact having examined this 2008 statement during the break you came back and confirmed that this was accurate in court. You say: "I refer to Major Ivan Juric. Even to this day I do not know what his real role was. He seemed to have both a command role and that of a coordinator. According to the organisational structure Budimir was my superior although I think I may have seen an order stating that all the military police units would be put at the disposal of Major Juric. " So clearly what you're saying is you say "I do not know what his real role was." Now, what happened or what material was placed before you from the point you made this statement which you confirm in court as accurate and yesterday when you agreed with Mr. Kay's suggestion that Major Juric was the commander of the military police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: -- in the zones of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, apparently the issue is repeatedly the same, that the way in which you present the evidence is contested by the Defence. So, therefore, if you just read literally what the testimony was, then --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll do that, Mr. President. I was in fact reading it because I had just taken down the exact notes. But I will read it now from the transcript so that we don't quarrel anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I add here too -- maybe the witness should take his headphones off again because I -- I know we all agree about the nature of this kind of question, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, could you take off again your earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I will be very brief so that we can move ahead. Ms. Mahindaratne knows exactly why the witness responded as he did because certain documents were put in front of him so that should be made clear to him so that he doesn't misunderstand what is actually being put to him, that Mr. Kay put a number of documents to him with which he then responded with certain answers, having seen those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that of course raises the question whether he is interpreting the documents or whether he is giving the answer. So, therefore, if Ms. Mahindaratne would put to the witness that after certain documents have been shown to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. But she doesn't have to put these documents again to him and can put her questions on the basis of just the recollection of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, for the Gotovina Defence I would say that I believe it is improper impeachment given that in the statement he says he seemed to have both a command role and that of a coordinator it would be improper impeachment then to it to the witness as if the witness has said something contradictory of the Prosecution's own witness when -- rather than just asking him to clarify. It shouldn't be put to him that he has said something inconsistent if in the statement he says he seemed to have both a command role that of a coordinator. I don't see the inconsistency, so I'm not sure if the witness would either and it should be put to him more fairly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- he clear says that even to this date he does not what the real role of Major Juric is, and my question would be what material or based on what material is he now agreeing with the suggestion made by the Defence and that is not necessarily impeachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think it is impeachment. Of course if you say it seems to be this and that, that is already different from what someone knows. It looks as if he is drawing conclusions on what he now sees or -- but no thorough knowledge. Put it as neutral as possible, ask for clarifications or explanations and do not put too many suggestions in your question, because that would be leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would also say again in fairness to the witness, Your Honour, he did testify that he received orders and specified at least one order that he received from Major Juric, so again I would say that it shouldn't be put to him that he is saying something inconsistent if in fact he believed that Juric could command him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will phrase it according to your instructions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, now, yesterday you agreed with the suggestion from the Defence that -- to read the exact words the suggestion was: "Would you agree he was," referring to Major Juric, "the commander of the military police in the zones of responsibility of the 72nd and 73rd at the time?" And your response was yes. Now you agreed with that suggestion. And previously you had informed the Office of the Prosecutor that you were not aware of what his real role was. Now can you explain to Court, Mr. Dzolic, what it was that led you to agree with the suggestion in Court, whereas on 20th August you did not know what the role of Major Juric was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Judge, I have the same objection. If she is going to put it to him, then she should show him paragraph 11 in its entirety and not select a sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And we join that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, could you show the witness what he said, at least take him to the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, can you look at your paragraph 11 of 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now you say there: "I refer to Major Ivan Juric. Even to this day, I do not know what his real role was." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will move on, Mr. President, from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So there is no further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so there is no further dispute later on when the transcript is read, I'm not sure that we interpret his yes -- she put it to him that's what it says, so that is what it says, we with stipulate that that's what it says in paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, when you said that is correct, were you agreeing that what I read to you says exactly that in the paragraph, or when you said that is correct, is it correct that you do not know what Major Ivan Juric real role was?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to what it says in paragraph 11. I said that it's correct that that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you agree with that statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made this statement in context, because I didn't know which role of Major Juric was more prominent, whether on the ground his role was that of commander or that of coordinator, which was the predominant role.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll move on from that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, your testimony was that you received your orders from Colonel Budimir, and in fact in paragraph 35 of the 2008 statement, if I could ask to you look at your 2008 statement, Mr. Dzolic, paragraph 35. You say: "All my orders from my battalion commander Colonel Budimir were delivered verbally. I cannot recall him ever informing me that an order had been issued by General Gotovina to prevent or investigate crimes. I wish to add that Colonel Budimir had sufficient authority that he did not have to use the name of Gotovina to get things done." Now, when -- when Colonel Budimir issued you verbal orders, did he ever inform you that he was issued any orders pursuant to General Gotovina's orders?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
